copy.title: The Arnault Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of Bernard Arnault’s family: who runs what at LVMH, which stocks you can buy, Paris FC, and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #015 · The Arnault family · Data as of
copy.h1: Five heirs, one luxury empire. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, what each of them runs, which of their companies you can buy stock in, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file: what they run, what’s on the record, and where every fact comes from. All five children work in the LVMH group.
copy.investLede: Two family companies trade in Paris: LVMH and the family holding company Christian Dior SE. Paris FC and the rest are privately owned.
copy.moneyLede: Almost all of it is LVMH stock, held through family companies. Forbes publishes one figure for Bernard and his family together.
copy.recordLede: The money that shows up in market filings, deals and gifts. Filings and reporting, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From his father’s construction firm to control of LVMH and its 75 houses.

summary.t: Chairman and CEO of LVMH since 1989, the year he became its majority shareholder. The group has 75 houses, including Louis Vuitton, Sephora and Tiffany.

owns.t: Through Christian Dior SE and Financière Agache, the family passed 50% of LVMH’s shares in February 2026, with 65.94% of the votes, according to filings with France’s market regulator.
The listed family holding company. In September 2026 the family proposed merging its other holdings into it and renaming it Agache SCA, which would then own 49.76% of LVMH and 65.55% of the votes.
His family holding. In December 2022 he turned it into a partnership limited by shares. His five children each own 20% of Agache Commandite, the company that can one day replace him at its head.
Agache backs the venture capital firm Aglaé Ventures, which has invested in Netflix and TikTok owner ByteDance.

record.t: Put up $15 million from his father’s construction business to buy Christian Dior in 1984.
LVMH bought Tiffany & Co. in 2021 for $15.8 billion, which Forbes says is believed to be the biggest luxury brand deal ever.
He and LVMH gave €200 million to restore Notre-Dame Cathedral after the 2019 fire. It reopened in December 2024.
In April 2025 LVMH raised the age limit for his combined chairman and CEO job to 85. It was the second time the limit went up.

facts.t: Forbes says his fortune peaked at about $233 billion. He lost nearly $50 billion in early 2026 as LVMH stock fell 26%.
LVMH made €80.8 billion in revenue and €10.9 billion in net profit in 2025, and proposed a €13 dividend per share.
Asked about succession at LVMH’s 2026 annual meeting, he said: “We’ll talk about this again in seven or eight years.”

kidsNote.t: Delphine and Antoine are from his first marriage; Alexandre, Frédéric and Jean are his sons with Hélène. All five work in the LVMH group.

summary.t: Canadian concert pianist who performs in Europe and North America as a soloist and chamber musician. She married Bernard in 1991. They have three sons: Alexandre, Frédéric and Jean.

facts.t: Her recordings with the pianist Louis Lortie won a Diapason d’Or.

summary.t: Chairman and CEO of Christian Dior Couture since February 2023. Before that she was an executive vice president at Louis Vuitton. She joined LVMH’s board in 2003, its first woman director.

worth.none: No separate estimate. Forbes counts the family’s fortune under Bernard.

owns.t: Runs Christian Dior Couture and sits on LVMH’s board and executive committee.
Owns 20% of Agache Commandite, like each of her siblings.

record.t: The siblings set up a rotating two-year chair for Agache Commandite, with Delphine taking it first.

facts.t: Founded the LVMH Prize for young fashion designers in 2014.

summary.t: Heads image and sustainability at LVMH and runs the family holding company Christian Dior SE. He earlier ran Berluti and became chairman of Loro Piana in 2013.

worth.none: No separate estimate. Forbes counts the family’s fortune under Bernard.

owns.t: Chairman and CEO of the listed family holding; named its chief executive in December 2022.
Board member. Presented the group’s environmental results at the 2026 annual meeting.
AFP called him the club’s future strongman when the family took control in November 2024.

facts.t: Married to the model Natalia Vodianova since 2020.

summary.t: Deputy CEO of Moët Hennessy, LVMH’s wines and spirits arm, since February 2025. Before that he was an executive vice president at Tiffany and ran the luggage maker Rimowa from 2016 to 2020.

worth.none: No separate estimate. Forbes counts the family’s fortune under Bernard.

owns.t: Board member and the No. 2 executive at Moët Hennessy.

facts.t: Studied at École Polytechnique, like his father.

summary.t: CEO of the cashmere label Loro Piana since June 2025. He ran TAG Heuer from 2020 and then LVMH Watches, which includes TAG Heuer, Hublot and Zenith.

worth.none: No separate estimate. Forbes counts the family’s fortune under Bernard.

owns.t: Managing director of Financière Agache, a family holding, and owns 20% of Agache Commandite.

summary.t: The youngest of the five. Director of marketing and development for Louis Vuitton’s watches since August 2021. He studied at MIT and Imperial College London.

worth.none: No separate estimate. Forbes counts the family’s fortune under Bernard.

companies.name: LVMH
companies.who: Family (about 50% of shares, 66% of votes) · Bernard (chairman & CEO) · four of the children (board)
companies.t: The family passed 50% of the shares in February 2026. LVMH had €80.8 billion in revenue in 2025 across 75 houses.

companies.name: Christian Dior SE
companies.t: The family’s listed holding company for LVMH shares. Outsiders own 2.44%, worth about €1.63 billion. The family plans to offer cash for those shares in early 2027 and rename the company Agache SCA.

companies.name: Paris FC
companies.t: Agache took 52.4% of the club in November 2024, with Red Bull holding 10.6%. L’Équipe estimated the investment at €100 to €200 million over several years.

companies.name: Aglaé Ventures
companies.t: Venture capital firm with investments in companies such as Netflix and ByteDance.
